name: sqlparser
license_evidence: LICENSE.TXT in the pinned crate (SHA-256 a60eea817514531668d7e00765731449fe14d059d3249e0bc93b36de45f759f2); Cargo.toml license = Apache-2.0
dependencies: sqlparser_derive 0.7.0 (visitor derive macros, enabled by the visitor feature)
scope: One SQL statement from local UTF-8 text with GenericDialect; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary. Other dialects are untested.
family_note: Parser::parse_sql tokenizes (src/tokenizer.rs) and parses (src/parser/mod.rs) into the src/ast types. The adapter reads Statement::Query (Select projection, from/joins, selection, group_by, order_by) and Statement::Insert (table, columns, VALUES rows) and walks relations and expressions through the crate's visitor API. Shared family: datafusion-sql, gluesql, polyglot-sql forks and the sqlparser-rs WASM npm packages build on it; the Python sqloxide binding also wraps it.

popularity.limitation: Includes transitive downloads through DataFusion and other query engines.

name: pg_query
license_evidence: Cargo.toml license = MIT in the pinned crate (checked in the image); the crate ships no license file. The vendored libpg_query is BSD-3-Clause upstream with PostgreSQL License code
dependencies: libpg_query C (vendored, built by build.rs with cc)
scope: One SQL statement from local UTF-8 text with the default PostgreSQL grammar; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary. Other parser modes are untested.
family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
family_note: pg_query::parse passes the text to the vendored libpg_query (pg_query_parse_protobuf_opts: the PostgreSQL scanner and bison grammar) and decodes the protobuf parse tree with prost. The adapter reads SelectStmt and InsertStmt fields and walks RangeVar, FuncCall, JoinExpr and A_Const nodes. Shared family with the C libpg_query path (same 18.1.0 grammar; the C control reaches the same 493 gram.c lines), Go pg_query_go, Python pglast and JavaScript libpg-query; metrics are not combined.

popularity.limitation: Counts include pulls by dependent crates (for example Postgres tooling built on pg_query).

name: sqlite3-parser
license_evidence: Cargo.toml license = Apache-2.0/MIT in the pinned crate; the shipped LICENSE file (SHA-256 88d9b4eb60579c191ec391ca04c16130572d7eedc4a86daa58bf28c6e14c9bcd) is a public-domain dedication
input_api: lexer::sql::Parser::new(&Bump, local bytes) and FallibleIterator::next -> Option<Cmd>
scope: One SQL statement from local bytes with the SQLite grammar; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary. String literals are kept as quoted tokens in the AST and unquoted by the adapter. Other SQLite syntax is untested.
family: SQLite grammar (lemon-rs port of SQLite's Lemon parse.y)
family_note: The build script compiles the bundled rlemon and generates parse.rs (Lemon LALR tables and the parse.y reduce actions written in Rust) into OUT_DIR; src/lexer/sql/mod.rs drives the hand-written tokenizer and the generated parser and yields Cmd values. The adapter reads Stmt::Select (columns, FromClause and its JoinedSelectTable list, where_clause, group_by, order_by) and Stmt::Insert (table name, column list, VALUES rows) and walks Expr for function names and Literal values. Same grammar as the SQLite C engine, which the oracle uses only through sqlite3_prepare; that engine exposes no syntax tree. libsql-sqlite3-parser, turso_sqlite3_parser, limbo_sqlite3_parser and oxisqlite-sqlite3-parser are forks of this crate.

popularity.limitation: Counts include downloads pulled in by dependent crates; the libsql and turso forks are counted separately.

name: qusql-parse
license_evidence: LICENSE.TXT in the pinned crate (SHA-256 a60eea817514531668d7e00765731449fe14d059d3249e0bc93b36de45f759f2, Apache License 2.0); Cargo.toml license = Apache-2.0
scope: One SQL statement from local UTF-8 text with the default MariaDB dialect; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary. Any error-level Issue fails the adapter, since the parser recovers from errors. Other dialects are untested.
family: qusql-parse hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser
family_note: parse_statements runs the crate's own lexer (src/lexer.rs) and parser (src/parser.rs, src/select.rs, src/insert_replace.rs) into typed statement and expression structs. The adapter reads Select and InsertReplace fields and walks the tree with the crate's Visitor (TableReference::Table/Join, Function and AggregateFunction calls, Integer/Float/String literals; numbers as span text). sql-parse, the predecessor crate by the same author, says it moved into qusql-parse and is excluded as a predecessor name.

popularity.limitation: Small absolute count; the predecessor sql-parse crate (746) is counted separately and not selected.

name: spg-sql
license_evidence: Cargo.toml license = MIT OR Apache-2.0 in the pinned crate (checked in the image); the crate ships no license file
scope: One SQL statement from local UTF-8 text with the crate's PostgreSQL-dialect grammar; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary. Other syntax is untested.
family: spg-sql hand-written PostgreSQL-dialect lexer and recursive-descent parser
family_note: parse_statement runs the crate's own lexer (src/lexer.rs) and parser (src/parser.rs) into its AST (src/ast.rs); it has no dependencies and does not use libpg_query or sqlparser-rs. It is the SQL front-end of the SPG database, published as a separate no_std crate. The adapter reads Select and Insert fields and walks Expr; COUNT(*) appears as a FunctionCall named count_star.

popularity.limitation: Small absolute count; most downloads likely come from the SPG database crates.

name: nom-sql
license_evidence: LICENSE in the pinned crate (SHA-256 8ac042195bf72b46a1e09f8a96bdb3e4a3ead3a3cb8d818771e3459f6d265c39, MIT License); Cargo.toml license = MIT
scope: One SQL statement from local bytes; valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls, each equal to the hand-written oracle summary. The last release is from 2020; other syntax is untested.
family_note: parse_query_bytes runs nom 5 combinators (src/parser.rs, select.rs, insert.rs, condition.rs, common.rs) into the crate's own AST. It is unrelated to sqlparser-rs. The adapter reads SelectStatement and InsertStatement fields and walks ConditionExpression trees; COUNT(*) is FunctionExpression::CountStar and decimals are Real {integral, fractional}. The last release, 0.0.11, is from 2020.

popularity.limitation: Small absolute count for an unmaintained 2020 release.
